name: Lunar south pole
desc: Rugged crater rims beside permanently shadowed craters that trap water ice. Low sun, extreme cold, anorthosite crust.

measured.v: Sunlit rims stay near 220 K (−53 °C) almost constantly; shadowed craters reach 25 K
measured.src: LRO Diviner

measured.v: Diviner temperatures cold enough to trap ice; LEND neutron data show ice likely, not only in permanent shadow
measured.src: NASA LRO fact sheet

measured.v: Measured by us over a 20 km circle at the pole: mean slope 23.5° at 313 m pixels (Shackleton is 21 km wide and 4.2 km deep)
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

measured.v: Measured by us: 164 ppm hydrogen, 2-3 times the other Moon targets (53-77 ppm), consistent with buried water ice
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

measured.v: Measured by us: FeO 6.4 wt%, iron-poor highland crust
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

name: Mare Imbrium plains
desc: Flat, dark basalt lava plains. The safest kind of lunar landing terrain, with huge day–night temperature swings.

measured.v: Low latitudes: ~387–397 K at noon, ~95 K before dawn, a swing of about 300 K
measured.src: Williams et al. 2017, Icarus (Diviner)

measured.v: Measured by us over a 20 × 20 km box: mean slope 0.54° at 313 m pixels
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

measured.v: Measured by us: FeO 21.1 wt%, iron-rich mare basalt
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
desc: A pit about 100 m deep that may open into a lava tube: natural shelter from radiation and temperature swings.

measured.v: About 100 m deep with an overhang; shaded parts stay near 17 °C while the surface ranges from −173 to 127 °C
measured.src: Horvath et al. 2022, GRL (Diviner)

measured.v: Measured by us over a 20 × 20 km box: mean slope 0.56° at 313 m pixels; the plains around the pit are very flat
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

measured.v: Measured by us: FeO 18.4 wt%, iron-rich mare basalt
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

name: Descartes highlands
desc: Bright, heavily cratered anorthosite crust: the oldest surface rocks on the Moon.

measured.v: Low latitudes: ~387–397 K at noon, ~95 K before dawn
measured.src: Williams et al. 2017, Icarus (Diviner)

measured.v: Anorthositic highland breccias returned by Apollo 16; measured by us: FeO 7.7 wt%, iron-poor
measured.src: Apollo 16 samples; LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

measured.v: Measured by us over a 20 × 20 km box: mean slope 4.0° at 313 m pixels
measured.src: LROC QuickMap Inspect (LOLA terrain, Lunar Prospector), measured by our team

name: Jezero Crater
desc: An ancient lake crater with a river delta, clays and carbonates. A top target in the search for signs of past life.

measured.v: Air averages about −55 °C, with day–night differences of 50–60 °C
measured.src: Perseverance MEDA (Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023, Nat. Geosci.)

measured.v: Measured by us over 20 × 20 km: mean slope 2.9° at 463 m pixels (MOLA), used for scoring; 5.8° at 20 m pixels from the USGS CTX slope map, showing how slope grows at finer scale
measured.src: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 px/deg (PDS), measured by our team in Google Colab; USGS Astrogeology CTX slope map

measured.v: Delta and lake deposits with clays and carbonates mapped from orbit
measured.src: MRO CRISM, HiRISE (Stack et al. 2020)

name: Gale Crater
desc: Layered sediments in Mount Sharp record a lake that dried out, leaving clays and sulfate salts.

measured.v: Equatorial Mars: mean temperatures far below any Earth desert, swings of tens of °C (as measured at Jezero)
measured.src: Rover weather stations (REMS, MEDA)

measured.v: Clay- and sulfate-bearing layers of Mount Sharp
measured.src: MRO CRISM; Curiosity

measured.v: Measured by us over 20 × 20 km on the flank of Mount Sharp: mean slope 13.4° at 463 m pixels
measured.src: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 px/deg (PDS), measured by our team in Google Colab

name: Arcadia Planitia
desc: Smooth mid-latitude plains with water ice just below the surface. A leading candidate area for a crewed base.

measured.v: Radar, thermal, neutron and image data combined into maps of buried ice across the mid-latitudes; widespread excess ice in Arcadia
measured.src: SWIM project (Morgan et al. 2021, Nat. Astron.)

measured.v: Measured by us over 20 × 20 km: mean slope 0.35° at 463 m pixels, elevation −3.9 km; very smooth plains
measured.src: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 px/deg (PDS), measured by our team in Google Colab

name: Arsia Mons pits
desc: Pit craters on the flanks of a giant shield volcano that may open into lava tubes, at very high altitude.

measured.v: Seven skylights 100–225 m across and at least 68–130 m deep; their day–night temperature change is about a third of the surface's
measured.src: Cushing et al. 2007, GRL (Mars Odyssey THEMIS)

measured.v: Measured by us over 20 × 20 km: elevation +16.4 km, mean slope 1.4° at 463 m pixels
measured.src: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 px/deg (PDS), measured by our team in Google Colab

name: Meridiani Planum
desc: Flat plains of sulfate-rich sandstone dotted with hematite spherules, nicknamed blueberries.

measured.v: Coarse-grained hematite detected from orbit; sulfate sandstones confirmed by Opportunity
measured.src: MGS TES; Opportunity

measured.v: Measured by us over 20 × 20 km: mean slope 0.32° at 463 m pixels; one of the flattest places on Mars
measured.src: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 px/deg (PDS), measured by our team in Google Colab
